name: The Lurkers
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: Four pub regulars from Ickenham rehearsed in a record shop basement, and the shop started a label to put them out. Beggars Banquet's first record is a Lurkers single, cut in an hour and a half.

hero.by: Photo: Man Alive! (Arturo Bassick with the Lurkers, Bangor, 2013)

eras.title: Out of the Coach & Horses
eras.text: The Lurkers were mates from the Coach & Horses in Ickenham, West London, with long hair, flares and a Ramones habit. They never bothered with safety pins. What they had was songs, a record shop basement to rehearse in, and a shop owner willing to start a label for them.

years.h: Plug can't sing, so Howard Wall has a go
years.p: [[Pete Stride|b5fb9532-783e-496e-868a-19d12137fa18]], Nigel Moore, drummer Pete 'Manic Esso' Haynes and singer Pete 'Plug' Edwards start the band. By the end of 1976 Howard Wall has the mic and Plug is the roadie.
years.xp:
Plug told Zigzag in 1979 that they only started it for a laugh: "I just wasn't good enough. Howard said he'd have a go and that's how the Lurkers began." He stayed on the road with them and played harmonica on a few tracks, including 'Suzie Is a Floozie'.

Esso explained the name to Sounds in 1978: they lurk, they won't follow anybody's fashions, and the Clash were posers.

years.cap: The Lurkers live under Beggars Banquet's 'Streets' banners
years.h: First gig: Uxbridge Tech, opening for Screaming Lord Sutch, to ten people
years.p: The Lurkers play their first show at Uxbridge Technical College. Within weeks they are among the early bands at the Roxy in Covent Garden.

years.h: Arturo Bassick gets the job in two minutes, without ever having played bass
years.p: Moore leaves for Swank and French Lessons before the Roxy debut. Arthur Billingsley, renamed Arturo Bassick, looks the part and gets hired on the spot.
years.xp:
"I got the job within 2 minutes of auditioning for them," Bassick told Punk 77. He'd been following The Stranglers since November 1976 and knew their management, who ran the Red Cow, the Nashville and the Hope and Anchor. That got the Lurkers support slots with the Stranglers and [[The Jam|23228f18-01d5-493e-94ce-cfcde82a8db2]].

Not every gig was in London: Punk 77 lists a handful of dates on the Isle of Arran, with no alcohol.

years.big: "It was recorded in one and a half hours."
q: It was recorded in one and a half hours.
years.src: Punk 77 · Beggars Group · Wikipedia: Beggars Banquet
yt: 'Shadow', live at the Red Cow, September 7, 1977
years.h: 'Shadow' becomes Beggars Banquet's first record
years.p: Bassick on 'Shadow' / 'Love Story', catalogue number BEG 1. The band rehearsed under Beggars Banquet's Fulham shop, and the shop started a label to release them.
years.xp:
Shop manager Mike Stone had become their manager. Nobody else was offering a deal, so Beggars put the single out themselves. Martin Mills called it an unusual thing to do then: "There were no small independent record companies."

Bassick remembered the engineer couldn't believe the speed; Rick Wakeman had just spent three weeks getting his keyboard sound right. Stride's one-note opening riff did the rest.

On September 7, 1977 the band played 'Shadow' at the Red Cow in Hammersmith for the cameras of the documentary Punk in London.

years.src: John Peel Wiki · Punk 77 · Damaged Goods
years.h: John Peel books the first of four sessions
years.p: Maida Vale, five songs: 'Freak Show', 'Total War', 'I'm on Heat', 'Then I Kissed Her', 'Be My Prisoner'. Peel puts 'Shadow' at 12 and 'Love Story' at 31 in his 1977 Festive Fifty.
years.xp: Three more sessions followed in April 1978, July 1978 and January 1979. Years later Peel admitted the band got sniffed at: "Punks with A levels tended to be a bit dismissive of the Lurkers." He liked Status Quo too, he said, and he liked the Lurkers.

years.h: Bassick writes 'Mass Media Believer', then leaves to start Pinpoint
years.p: His song is the B-side of 'Freak Show', BEG 2. Kym Bradshaw, ex-The Saints, takes over on bass.

eras.title: Five chart singles, none higher than 45
eras.text: Backed by Beggars Banquet and the distribution muscle of WEA, the Lurkers had five chart singles and a chart album in about 18 months, a Top of the Pops slot and a hardcore following called the Fulham Boys. None of the singles got past number 45.

years.cap: Beggars Banquet advert for 'Ain't Got a Clue', 1978
years.h: Kym Bradshaw is out for being 'too professional'
years.p: Nigel Moore returns on bass. The NME's character sketch said he got the job back partly because he had a car and was the only one who could drive.
years.xp:
Bradshaw's version, to Punk 77 in 2003: he was "sacked officially because I was 'too professional'", and he thought Stride didn't like him starting to write better songs.

Stride's version, to the NME in June 1978: they were chuffed at first to land a big-name bass player, but offstage Bradshaw "turned out to be really straight... Kym was like a married man."

years.h: Fulham Fallout charts at 57, in a gatefold sleeve
years.p: Like Never Mind the Bollocks, it collects reworked singles and fills out the live set. Only Bassick was actually from Fulham; the title is for their fans there.
years.xp: The Fulham Boys came from Kingston, Southall and Fulham. "Most of them just like us and no other band," Moore told the NME. Wall told Sounds that a gig in Bradford felt flat until the Fulham kids turned up.

yt: 'I Don't Need to Tell Her' on Top of the Pops, 1978
years.h: 'I Don't Need to Tell Her' gets them on Top of the Pops
years.p: The single reaches 49, just behind 'Ain't Got a Clue', their biggest hit at 45. They also play it on ITV's Revolver, filmed July 22, 1978.

years.h: 'Just Thirteen' stalls at 66 and outlives the chart
years.p: BEG 14. Mojo picked it in 2001 for its list of the 100 best punk singles. Around the same time a headlining night at London's Lyceum, with crowds of up to 1,500, turned into a string of fights.

years.h: A London punk band flies to Muscle Shoals to make album two
years.p: Beggars sends them to Alabama with producer Phillip Jarrell, whose background was Motown acts. Punk 77 says the sessions were full of personality clashes.
years.xp: The other problem, per Punk 77: a band who liked a pint found themselves in dry territory, and solved it with regular three-hour drives over the state line for supplies.

years.h: God's Lonely Men slows down and toughens up
years.p: Less frantic than the debut, more hard rock, with Stride's songwriting stretching out. Money went into making and promoting it; it didn't chart.
years.xp: Punk 77 adds that Howard Wall was hospitalised in 1979 with suspected meningitis, put down to spit from the crowd; two years earlier punk bashers had beaten him up on a bus.

years.h: 'Honest' John Plain of The Boys comes in on second guitar
years.p: Plain plays on 'New Guitar in Town', which reaches 72. The band promote it with four nights at the Marquee.

eras.title: Dropped, split, and rebooted in Stoke
eras.text: By 1980 the scene had moved on to Oi, Gary Numan and the New Romantics. Punk 77 says the Lurkers were dropped, heavily in debt to the label, and drifted apart. Stride brought the name back on a small label in Stoke-on-Trent.

years.h: Beggars Banquet drops the Lurkers and the band drift apart
years.p: Stride makes an album with John Plain, released in January 1980. Beggars puts out a greatest-hits set, Last Will and Testament, in November.

years.h: Mike Stone brings the Lurkers back on Clay Records
years.p: Their old manager now runs Clay in Stoke-on-Trent. Stride, Moore and Esso return with new singer Marc Fincham and 'This Dirty Town'. The Clay years yield four singles and one album, This Dirty Town (1983), before a second split in 1984.

eras.title: Arturo's Lurkers
eras.text: In 1987 Arturo Bassick revived the name and ran the band for 34 years, with Stride and Moore at first and then a rotating cast. That version toured hard, especially in Germany, and made records for small European labels.

years.src: God's Lonely Men · Wikipedia: The Lurkers
years.h: Campino of [[Die Toten Hosen|c3bc80a6-1f4a-4e17-8cf0-6b1efe8302f1]] puts on a Lurkers show in Düsseldorf
years.p: Bassick fronts a new line-up with Stride, Moore and drummer Dan Tozer. Wild Times Again follows on Weser in 1988.
years.xp: Bassick ran this version for 34 years with a rotating cast. In January 2009 it opened for [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]] on 14 UK dates.

eras.title: Two Lurkers, one name
eras.text: Stride, Moore and Esso reunited as God's Lonely Men, then took the Lurkers name back while Bassick's version was still touring. Nobody sued; they'd been friends for forty years.

years.src: Damaged Goods · God's Lonely Men · Louder Than War
years.h: Three originals return as God's Lonely Men with Chemical Landslide
years.p: Heavier than the old records. The Future's Calling follows in 2016 on Unlatched.

years.h: "That's not very very punk!" Jordan tells Esso at the Roxy plaque
years.p: Esso nearly skips the blue plaque unveiling for the Roxy Club. He turns up in a football shirt, and Jordan quizzes him on who he is.

years.src: Louder Than War · Damaged Goods · Wikipedia: The Lurkers
years.h: High Velocity comes out under the Lurkers name, on pink vinyl
years.p: 500 copies on Human Punk/Damaged Goods, with the Featherz singer Danie Cox as guest. Bassick had been touring as the Lurkers since 1987.
years.xp:
Louder Than War noted the two camps had been friends for over 40 years and weren't expected to go to court over it. Its verdict on the record: ramalama punk pop, the way they used to make it.

Cox, renamed Danie Centric, joined full time in February 2018 while staying in the Featherz. In January 2019 'Electrical Guitar' topped the UK Official Vinyl Singles chart.

years.h: Bassick folds his Lurkers after 34 years to concentrate on 999
years.p: His version had played its last gigs in March 2020. That leaves the Stride, Moore and Esso line-up as the only Lurkers.

years.h: The 1977 demos come out 46 years late, and chart at number two
years.p: Damaged Goods issues the first demos on 7-inch alongside a three-CD box, then a live set from the Queens Hotel in Margate, December 23, 1977.

sources.title: Louder Than War: The Lurkers, High Velocity
